papers.key_finding: Diffusion equilibrates in systems whose reaction networks are pseudo-detailed balanced or complex balanced, with distinct constraints on reaction fluxes arising from stoichiometric properties.
papers.title: Identifying Non-Ideal Reaction-Diffusion Systems Unable to Maintain Diffusion Out-of-Equilibrium
papers.tldr: The authors develop a method using a kinetic potential as a Lyapunov function to identify conditions under which diffusion equilibrates in non-ideal reaction-diffusion systems driven by chemostats, generalizing previous results by relaxing assumptions.
papers.why_relevant: This work advances the systems-theoretic understanding of non-equilibrium reaction-diffusion systems, which is foundational for your research on binding–catalysis systems and stochastic limits in biomolecular control.

papers.key_finding: Receptor architecture with multi-step phosphorylation and proofreading allows signaling activity and range to increase together over a finite window of ligand residence time, overcoming the canonical synthesis-diffusion-degradation tradeoff.
papers.title: Kinetic proofreading decouples signal strength and range in paracrine gradient formation
papers.tldr: The authors propose a model of multi-step ligand processing with kinetic-proofreading-like resetting that decouples signal strength from spatial range in paracrine gradient formation, explaining recent live-imaging data for EGF receptor ligands.
papers.why_relevant: This paper provides a mechanistic example of kinetic proofreading in spatial signaling, directly relevant to your research on sensing and proofreading in biological systems.

papers.key_finding: The model uses Hamilton's principle for thermodynamic consistency and can qualitatively reproduce complex interaction patterns, including spatial structure and population dynamics.
papers.title: A continuum multi-species bacterial growth model with a novel interaction scheme
papers.tldr: The authors present a continuum multi-species bacterial biofilm model that incorporates arbitrary species interactions, nutrient and antibiotic effects, and is thermodynamically consistent via derivation from Hamilton's principle.
papers.why_relevant: This thermodynamic, continuum modeling approach for bacterial populations aligns with your interest in dynamic metabolism and bacterial physiology, offering a framework for mathematical biology methods.

papers.key_finding: A heuristic-based algorithm efficiently finds local solutions for positive linear systems, and a distributed algorithm provides local controllers within an optimality bound with a termination condition.
papers.title: Heuristic search for linear positive systems
papers.tldr: The authors show an equivalence between stochastic shortest path problems and optimal control of a class of positive linear systems, and derive heuristic search algorithms for distributed local control with performance bounds.
papers.why_relevant: This advances control-theoretic tools for positive systems, which are relevant to your work on systems theory and computational design for biomolecular and microbial systems.
